subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin, the least magically inclined member of the party, succeeds where all the spellcasters failed — correctly identifying the psychic center of the Hall of Melting Mirrors using a lucky roll and dwarvish intuition.
source_quote: Chipgrin remarks he should have asked the dwarf first, before awkwardly clarifying to Zalthir that he meant no offense by calling them a 'surface dweller'.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Explaining the origin of his mysterious bone die after using it to pacify an entire army of oozes through Glabbagool.
source_quote: The old mule swore it was carved from the knucklebone of a saint who never told a lie, said it had a memory for the truth. I thought he was just trying to cover his losses.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir uses a special ability to inspect Jimjar and discovers he possesses divine-level immunities and resistances. Jimjar notices, winks, and vanishes into thin air — hinting the party will meet again.
source_quote: The party had long suspected Jimjar was more than he appeared; this confirmed it, with his stat block resembling that of an angel or deity.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Juiblex was a loud, messy neighbor, but this sister, she prefers to move in while you're sleeping.
source_quote: Juiblex was a loud, messy neighbor, but this sister, she prefers to move in while you're sleeping.

subject: Hall of Melting Mirrors
fact: Chipgrin and his wererats had been maintaining a chanting vigil to suppress the lingering psychic static left behind by the mirrors.
source_quote: Chipgrin turned to the party's spellcasters, hoping one of them could locate the harmonic center of the room and silence the noise for good.

subject: bone die
fact: The die was won off a blind Duergar in Gracklstugh, claimed to have been carved from the knucklebone of a saint who never told a lie — a die with a memory for the truth.
source_quote: The old mule swore it was carved from the knucklebone of a saint who never told a lie, said it had a memory for the truth. I thought he was just trying to cover his losses.

subject: Voucher of the Varmint
fact: A braided rat's foot pressed into Daz's hand by Chief Chipgrin — a token recognized by wererats and outcasts from Blingdenstone all the way to Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: Chief Chipgrin pressed a braided rat's foot into Daz's hand — the Voucher of the Varmint, he called it, a token recognized by wererats and outcasts from Blingdenstone all the way to Menzoberranzan.

subject: Diggermattock Miners patch
fact: A patch sewn onto Thorin's gear by Diggermattock, declaring him an honorary member of the crew, later attached with divine precision by Grygum's cantrip.
source_quote: Diggermattock was so moved that he personally threaded a needle and sewed a Diggermattock Miners patch onto Thorin's gear, declaring him an honorary member of the crew. Grygum, not to be outdone, used a cantrip to attach the patch with such precision that everyone present was briefly more impressed by the needlework than by the feat of engineering.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar is immune to poison and psychic damage, cannot be charmed or frightened, shrugs off radiant energy and mundane weapons alike — a profile matching no ordinary gnome, and bearing a striking resemblance to something far more divine.
source_quote: Zalthir, long suspicious of the little gambler, reached out with a focused awareness and discovered that Jimjar was immune to poison and psychic damage, could not be charmed or frightened, and shrugged off radiant energy and mundane weapons alike — a profile that matched no ordinary gnome, and bore a striking resemblance to something far more divine.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool briefly became a bridge between every ooze in the cavern, a single vast mind connecting jellies, puddings, and cubes alike, and told them, in his gentle and earnest way, that the world was fine, that everyone could get along, and that there was really no need to kill anyone.
source_quote: Glabbagool briefly became a bridge between every ooze in the cavern, a single vast mind connecting jellies, puddings, and cubes alike. He told them, in his gentle and earnest way, that the world was fine, that everyone could get along, and that there was really no need to kill anyone.

subject: Blingdenstone
fact: The city sent the party off with ceremony: working-class gnomes lined the tunnels chanting their new rallying cry, the Burrow Warden ghosts dipped their spectral banners in salute, and legends of the Ember Vanguard were already spreading through the tunnels.
source_quote: Working-class gnomes lined the tunnels chanting their new rallying cry, the Burrow Warden ghosts dipped their spectral banners in salute, and Chief Chipgrin pressed a braided rat's foot into Daz's hand — the Voucher of the Varmint, he called it, a token recognized by wererats and outcasts from Blingdenstone all the way to Menzoberranzan.

subject: farming area beyond the tunnels
fact: A panicked gnome farmer warned the party that the city was under attack, and beyond the Trader's Grotto, a writhing, churning mass of oozes, jellies, and black puddings, no longer bound by the Pudding King's will and very unhappy about it.
source_quote: At the Trader's Grotto, they found a large Gnomish army standing before a breached wall, and beyond it — a writhing, churning mass of oozes, jellies, and black puddings, no longer bound by the Pudding King's will and very unhappy about it.

subject: support beams
fact: Gnomish miners were locked in a heated debate over construction materials and methods, arguing with the passionate conviction of people who had very strong opinions about zurkhwood versus steel.
source_quote: Gnomish miners were locked in a heated debate over construction materials and methods, arguing with the passionate conviction of people who had very strong opinions about zurkhwood versus steel.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar vanished entirely from existence, leaving only the faint metallic clink of platinum coins echoing in the tunnel behind him.
source_quote: Jimjar noticed the scrutiny, offered a knowing wink, and vanished entirely from existence, leaving only the faint metallic clink of platinum coins echoing in the tunnel behind him.

subject: pale white puffball mushroom
fact: A pale white puffball mushroom growing at impossible speed from a crack in the wall, its scent cloyingly sweet, like a feast left to rot in a hothouse — a sign of Zuggtmoy's quiet infiltration.
source_quote: Jimjar pointed to a pale white puffball mushroom growing at impossible speed from a crack in the wall, its scent cloyingly sweet, like a feast left to rot in a hothouse.

subject: Blingdenstone factions
fact: The various factions of Blingdenstone — miners, wererats, ghosts, and spiritual leaders — were already at each other's throats over the future of the city.
source_quote: The party worked the room with careful insight: they brokered a wage agreement between the miners guild and the working class, proposed that the Gold Whisker wererats take control of the upper boroughs as a self-funded defense force, and helped broker a compromise on sustainable mining practices that satisfied both the Miners Guild and the ghosts who considered the sanctum sacred ground.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum tended to the miners who had suffered burns, used a cantrip to attach the Diggermattock Miners patch with divine precision, and paid ten platinum pieces without complaint.
source_quote: Grygum tended to the miners who had suffered burns, while Thorin threw his considerable strength into winching a critical support beam into place, aided by Daz's tactical guidance. Grygum, not to be outdone, used a cantrip to attach the patch with such precision that everyone present was briefly more impressed by the needlework than by the feat of engineering. Grygum paid the ten platinum pieces without complaint.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz stepped forward and delivered a passionate appeal for unity, urging the assembled leaders to set aside their egos and build an alliance strong enough to outlast the demons.
source_quote: Daz stepped forward and delivered a passionate appeal for unity, urging the assembled leaders to set aside their egos and build an alliance strong enough to outlast the demons.

subject: Chief Diggermattock
fact: Chief Diggermattock and Chipgrin were already arguing about how to divide the newly opened territory, seemingly unbothered by the fact that said territory was currently full of ooze.
source_quote: Chief Diggermattock and Chipgrin were already arguing about how to divide the newly opened territory, seemingly unbothered by the fact that said territory was currently full of ooze.

subject: Chipgrin
fact: Chipgrin turned to the party's spellcasters, hoping one of them could locate the harmonic center of the room and silence the noise for good, then muttered he probably should have asked the dwarf first.
source_quote: Chipgrin turned to the party's spellcasters, hoping one of them could locate the harmonic center of the room and silence the noise for good. Chipgrin stared at him for a long moment before muttering that he probably should have asked the dwarf first, then caught Zalthir's eye and hastily clarified that he meant no offense by that.

subject: Trader's Grotto
fact: A large Gnomish army stood before a breached wall, and beyond it — a writhing, churning mass of oozes, jellies, and black puddings, no longer bound by the Pudding King's will and very unhappy about it.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar approached Grygum and offered a bet of ten platinum pieces, claiming that Glabbagool — the party's intelligent gelatinous cube companion — had more sense than the Pudding King ever had.
source_quote: Jimjar approached Grygum and offered a bet of ten platinum pieces, claiming that Glabbagool — the party's intelligent gelatinous cube companion — had more sense than the Pudding King ever had.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar shrugged and said he had figured that in a place where the blink had turned the world's math into a bad joke, a little uncertainty could go a long way.
source_quote: Jimjar shrugged and said he had figured that in a place where the blink had turned the world's math into a bad joke, a little uncertainty could go a long way.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar tossed a small bone die onto Glabbagool. A strange blink rippled through the air, and then something extraordinary happened: Glabbagool briefly became a bridge between every ooze in the cavern.
source_quote: Jimjar tossed a small bone die onto Glabbagool. A strange blink rippled through the air, and then something extraordinary happened: Glabbagool briefly became a bridge between every ooze in the cavern, a single vast mind connecting jellies, puddings, and cubes alike.
